Hi everyone,

just a quick note following the recent supply delivery (PO-2025-1189). We would like to gently remind everyone to be mindful of how we use everyday office items such as like paper, pens, and whiteboard markers. While these are essentials, overuse or carelessness can lead to extra costs and waste.

Just a quick note following the recent supply delivery (PO-2025-1189). We would like to gently remind everyone to be mindful when using everyday office supplies such as paper, pens, and whiteboard markers. These items are essential, but excessive or careless use can lead to unnecessary costs and waste.

Here are a few simple ways to help out:

  • Think before you print. Use double-sided printing format. Go digital when possible.
  • Keep supplies tidy. Store pens, markers, and calendars properly so they do not get misplaced or damaged.
  • Request only what you need. No need to hoard. Supplies are restocked regularly and available as needed.
  • Return unused items. If something is neither used nor needed, give or send it back to the administration team so it can be reused.

Let’s all do our part in keeping the workplace efficient and eco-friendly. If you have questions or need something specific, just contact us at extension 221.

 

Thank you for your help,
Office Management Division
PT Vitasena Indonesia

Fat in Balanced Diet

Your diet must contain some fat, but you must be careful about the kind and quantity of fat you consume. Saturated and unsaturated fats are the two main kinds of fat. The risk of heart disease will get higher when blood cholesterol levels increase due to an extreme consumption of saturated fat.

Men need to consume a maximum of 30 grams of saturated fat per day on average, and women need less than 20 grams of saturated fat per day on average. Those under the age of 11 must have less saturated fat than adults, while kids under the age of 5 have to avoid a low-fat diet. For kids under two, full-fat dairy products like cheese and yogurt are recommended. Saturated fat can be discovered in a variety of foods, such as sausages, butter, hard cheese, cream, cakes, biscuits, and fatty meat cuts.

Consume more foods high in unsaturated fat, such as oily fish, vegetable oils, avocados, and spreads such as mayonnaise. For a healthier alternative to butter and palm oil, try just a little of vegetable or olive oil, or low-fat spread. Select lean cuts of meat and trim off any excess fat while eating it. Due to their high energy content, all types of fat should only be consumed in controlled amounts.

(Adapted from www.nhs.uk/live-well/eat-well/how-to-eat-a-balanced-diet/eight-tips-for-healthy-eating/)

My Internship Experience as a Nurse Assistant

Hello. My name is Sinta. I am majoring in Nursing Assistant at Semarang Health Vocational School. I would like to share my experience completing an internship at Sehati Hospital in Semarang from February 20th to May 20th. Five of my friends and I completed our internship there. Before I even started my internship, I already predicted that the experience would be exciting but challenging and wearying at the same time. At Sehati Hospital, we interned and learned in various places, including the nursery, the outpatient ward, the inpatient ward, the operating room, and the emergency room. After about two and a half weeks, we moved to a different room or division.

At first, I was assigned to the nursery, where I learned from senior nurses how to correctly and carefully bathe babies, prepare formula, wash bottles, change diapers, and educate new mothers on breastfeeding. Next, in the third week, when I was in the outpatient ward, I communicated directly with many patients. My duties included checking vital signs, assisting with medical record-keeping, collecting laboratory results, and preparing the doctor's office.

After around two and a half weeks in the outpatient ward. I interned in the inpatient ward where I learned a lot, especially about how to take vital signs such as blood pressure, breathing rate, and pulse, among other things. I enjoyed helping to check the vital signs of small children the most. On the days when I got the night shift, I felt that the atmosphere was very calming even though it was also rather longer than the day shif. There was also my experience when I got my turn in the operating and recovery rooms. In there, I observed newborn babies, cleaned medical equipment, and assisted with postpartum care for new mothers. Finally, for the last two and a half weeks of my internship, I had to assist with initial wound care in the emergency room. After that, I thoroughly finished my internship. My friend and I said goodbye and thanked the nurses, doctors, and hospital staff that had helped us so much during our internship period at Sehati Hospital.

The reality of my internship was as I predicted; that it would be stimulating while also being difficult and tiring. But it turned out that I was happy to do the work and activities. I loved it when patients showed their appreciation to me and my fellow interns, which really touched my heart. That was something I really looked forward to. Someday, when I earn my degree and become a licensed nurse, I will dedicate myself to contribute and to provide better healthcare.

(DC/100%/SST)

The Beauty of Bougainvillea

Bougainvillea is an ornamental plant that is well known in various regions of Indonesia. The actual flower of this plant is very small and right in the middle of the petals. However, people often consider the brightly colored petals as the flower itself because they are more eye-catching. Planting this flower is relatively easy, one of the methods being stem cuttings.

This plant is also called Paper Flower because its flowers are as smooth and thin as paper. Bougainvillea generally grows upright and has a relatively small shape. Its leaves are dark green, oval-shaped, and not sharply pointed at the tip. The beauty of this plant lies in its brightly colored petals which have with several color variations depending on the type. The trunk and branches are surrounded by thorns. Bougainvillea can grow more than 10 meters tall. The leaves are large, slightly pointed, and grow densely around the branches.

Bougainvillea originates from South America, but over time, it has spread widely to tropical regions such as Indonesia because it has high adaptability, is drought-tolerant, and requires optimal sunlight. It can grow almost in every season, which makes it possible to enjoy its beauty throughout the year.

Bandung Techno Park

Bandung Techno Park (BTP) is one of Indonesia’s most important places for new technology and innovation. It contains around 20 structures designed to support research and development, and it occupies about 50 hectares of land. Many technology companies and new start-ups choose BTP as their base because of its modern facilities.

One important area is the advanced materials laboratory, which stores and provides special tools for studying materials in great detail. This lab has equipment like powerful microscopes that can see things almost at the atomic level. As a result, researchers have made significant progress in developing new semiconductors and nanomaterials.

Next to it is the additive manufacturing center, which has large 3D printers that can make parts from plastics and metals. This enables companies to create and test new designs more quickly. For example, the center has made special medical implants that fit a patient’s body exactly. The life sciences research wing has high-security laboratories where scientists work on new medicines and study infectious diseases. These labs contributed significantly to the development of vaccines during the COVID-19 epidemic. The integration testing center allows different technologies such as smart city systems, renewable energy, and AI software to be tested together.

  BTP also supports green technology through the renewable energy testing facility. Here, companies can test solar panels, wind energy systems, and batteries in different conditions. For data work, the data analytics center has very fast computers that help researchers in areas like climate studies and artificial intelligence.

One of BTP’s strengths is that it is open for collaboration with universities to private companies all through straightforward and manageable administration and agreements. All BTP facilities follow ISO 9001:2015 standards, which means their work is high quality and trusted worldwide.

Sanur Beach

Sanur is considered one of Bali's most family-friendly places. The tranquil seashore town on Bali's southeast coast was one of the island's initial tourist destinations, and it remains popular for its amazing hotels, shopping, breakfast, massages, and easy access to the Nusa islands. Calm sea waves and shallow water surrounded by a line of offshore reefs make it a perfect swimming spot for children. In addition, the summer months of May to August bring a refreshing breeze.

There are also other enjoyable activities to do around there. The 7-kilometer-long shoreline with a paved footpath is ideal for a morning walk, jog, or even a bicycle ride. It's a beautiful scenic road surrounded by fishing boats, hotel gardens, and beach restaurants. The entire public beach area is free to enter, and loungers and bicycles may usually be rented for a low cost along the boardwalk.

Sanur Beach is one of Bali's most popular sites for swimming, snorkeling, and other varieties of water sports. The strong breeze makes it ideal for parasailing, kitesurfing, and windsurfing. You may also rent jet skis or banana boats. A variety of water sports are available at booths along the beach path. You can also try the Sea Walker for an interesting experience. It’s a safe and exciting underwater experience. You may not dive without a certification, but you can still get down to the sea floor up to 5-meter-deep to walk around exploring the underwater world and without getting your hair wet due to the innovative Sea Walker equipment.

The Origins of Cenderawasih

Once upon a time, in the Land of Papua, a couple named Bone and Baria were fishing on a river when they found a baby inside a floating basket. They took the baby as their son and named him Kweiya. A few years later, Baria gave birth to Niko and then Kiara. Kweiya, Niko, and Kiara were raised together in a house near a dense forest, Father Bone and Mother Baria treated their children equally. A good natured child, Keiya always diligently helped his parents by taking care of his two siblings, helping Father Bone with farming, and looking for fruits in the forest. Kweiya was remarkably spry in helping, such as when he nimbly climbed trees looking for fruits in the forest. Father Bone and Mother Baria complimented Kweiya on his diligence. Without their parents and Kweiya’s knowledge, this had made Niko and Kiara grow envious.

One day, Mother Baria fell ill. Father Bone had to stay home to take care of her and to harvest their farm. He asked his children to find red fruits to cure Mother Baria on the edges of the forest. Kweiya, Niko, and Kiara went to the forest. However, Niko and Kiara were secretly planning something. They persuaded Kweiya to go further into the forest. Kweiya was doubtful about their safety in the unknown part of the forest, but Niko and Kiara convinced him by spinning a story that the deepest part of the forest had more red fruits than other places in the forest. At first, the three of them went in together. Kweiya looked around in amazement at the beautiful scenery that he had never seen before. But then, Niko and Kiara left him when Kweiya was too engrossed in picking the red fruits.

Later, Kweiya felt that he had gotten enough red fruits and was about to go home, but the night had fallen. He couldn’t see the way back out of the forest. He was lost. Meanwhile back at home, his two siblings had returned and told their parents that Kweiya insisted on going into the deepest part of the forest. Father Bone and Mother Baria searched for Kweiya until dusk, but they couldn't find him.

Days went by and Kweiya was still never found. Mother Baria's health had declined further because she was agonizing over the loss while Father kept trying to look for Kweiya with Niko and Kiara accompanying him. One morning, Mother heard the door being knocked. She opened the door, looked out, and found no one except a pile of red fruits. Days afterward, piles of red fruits always suddenly appeared in front of the house. The family never saw who had brought the fruits. When Mother’s health finally recovered, she heard a trill of birdsong. Outside, there was a handsome bird with colorful feathers. It dropped red fruits to the ground. It sang again to her one last time and then flew away, never to be seen again.

How to Make Vegetable Scramble

Serving:        1-2 people

Ingredients:

  • 2 eggs
  • 2 teaspoons butter or olive oil
  • 1 small potato, diced
  • 2-3 tablespoons onion, finely crushed
  • 3 cloves garlic, finely crushed
  • 3-4 cherry tomatoes, roughly chopped
  • Salt and pepper, to taste
  • 2 handfuls of baby spinach, wash and drain

Preparations and Cooking:

  1. First, prepare all of your vegetables and spices. Prepare the egg too by cracking them into a bowl.
  2. Next, heat the oil or butter in a pan over medium-high heat until it’s sizzling.
  3. Then, put the potato in and increase the heat a little. Stir-fry the potato around three to five minutes. Check the tenderness; the potato is ready when you can easily stick it with a fork.
  4. After that, add the onion into the stir-fry. Stir again for another two minutes or until the onion becomes a bit brown. Add in the garlic and stir for a further minute. Then add the tomato and stir-fry about one more minute.
  5. When the stir-fry’s juice cooks off, finally take the stir-fry pan off the heat. Immediately add the eggs to the pan, then stir. As you mix, the remaining heat will quite cook the egg. Add salt and pepper to taste. If the egg is not fully cooked, put the pan back on very low heat, stir frequently, and slowly cook the scramble well done. This method keeps the egg tender and creamy.
  6. To finish, toss the spinach into the pan and stir until it wilts. You can also add it just before serving so that the spinach stays raw.
  7. Serve the vegetable scramble on top of toast, on top of rice, or with a salad of your choice.

My Interning Experience in MageHub

Hello, my name is Aidil. I am a student of the Visual Communication Design program at the state vocational high school’s Faculty of Fine Arts and Design. Last year, I interned at MageHub Indonesia. The internship lasted two months, taking place every weekday from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM on the MageHub Indonesia online platform.

I joined the internship with three other students from various programs and schools. My fellow interns and I had a training coordinator who served as a mentor during the internship. She assisted us with assignments and case study projects. She also connected us with trainers who would observe and assist the internship participants when we encountered obstacles or did not understand the material on the MageHub platform.

Interning students had to attend professional divisions according to their chosen programs, such as Game Designer, 2D Artist, 3D Artist, Animator, Audio Engineer, Game Tester, and many more. In this case, I chose the Art & Illustration, a part in Game Designer program. I was given a task to assist in creating a design for a character wearing traditional Indonesian costumes. We had to join daily assignments for training class requirements. To track my progress, we had to submit reports twice a day at ten in the morning and three in the afternoon. We did all of these activities online.

The training coordinator would assign a case study project to the students after completing the training class. The theme and level of difficulty of the project would be determined based on the participants' evaluation and work results in the training class. After completing the class and the project, students would write reports by filling out a feedback form and writing an article about their internship at MageHub Indonesia that aligned with their passions and was useful to readers.

Throughout the internship period, I learned about effective time management, tasks or projects on-time completion skills, and the importance of honesty along with responsibility that are required in the professional world. My internship experience at MageHub Indonesia was very memorable. Although the internship was conducted online, I still remember how I sometimes felt tired and dizzy because of the deadlines. I felt nervous and excited when our trainers commented on our tasks. The trainers’ comments greatly helped me develop the assigned case study project.

Elsa’s Online Bakery

Elsa, a grade 11 culinary student from Yogyakarta, had always loved baking. Her cookies were popular among friends and family, but she never thought of selling them—until her teacher assigned a project on small business development.

Elsa decided to give it a try. She baked a batch of chocolate chip cookies and posted a few photos on her Instagram account with the caption, “Homemade and fresh! DM to order.” She didn’t expect much, but within a few hours, she had five orders.

That weekend, she baked more cookies and started packaging them in simple boxes with hand-written thank-you notes. She called her brand Elsa’s Sweet Bites. Every evening after school, she baked and packed cookies, sometimes with help from her younger sister.

The orders kept coming. Her friends shared her posts, and even some teachers placed orders. Elsa learned how to calculate prices, manage time, and talk to customers. Once, she ran out of chocolate chips and had to explain a delay to a customer. She was nervous, but the customer understood. That moment taught her the importance of honesty and effective communication in business.

After three months, she had saved enough money to buy a new hand mixer. “It’s not just a project anymore,” she told her teacher. “It’s my business.”

Her teacher smiled. “That’s what entrepreneurship is all about. Starting small and growing with heart.”

Ayam Cincane: A Traditional Dish from Samarinda

Ayam Cincane is a traditional dish from Samarinda in East Kalimantan. The main ingredient is free-range chicken which has denser, chewier, and more fibrous meat. To cook Ayam Cincane, the chicken is cooked with an array of local spices, resulting in a savory and spicy flavor with a tender texture. The dish's tempting aroma is especially appealing when the chicken is later grilled over a charcoal or wood fire. Ayam Cincane is often served at special events such as weddings, religious ceremonies, and to welcome honored guests.

In addition to its delicious taste, Ayam Cincane is rich in nutrients. Free-range chicken—which is required in the recipe—is rich in protein, calcium, potassium, vitamins A and B?, and vital minerals like iron; all of which are very great for health. These nutrients help maintain bone health and bone mineral density, build muscle mass, reduce the risk of injury, and promote children's growth. All of those nutrients has benefits for pregnant and nursing women’s health. It is not an exaggeration to say that Ayam Cincane is medically beneficent as well as incredibly tasty.

Ayam Cincane also has an interesting history. People say this dish was first made in the Kutai Kartanegara Dynasty. It was first made by a chef named Cincane who worked at a palace. He mixed his own spices to make a new dish. The delicious and spicy flavors made the King of Kutai really like this dish. Because of this, Ayam Cincane became a favorite in the palace and has been enjoyed ever since. Today, Ayam Cincane is easy to find in restaurants, food stalls, and street vendors. It is also a highlight in festivals as a traditional delicacy.

(Adapted from www.kompasiana.com/ekasucicahyanii2753/67c1c98f34777c2f4700a8f2)

How to Grow Mung Beans in Pots

Materials Needed:

  • Small pots or containers
  • Planting soil
  • Green bean seeds
  • Watering can or spray bottle
  • Sunny windowsill or grow light
  • Notebook or growth chart

Steps:

To grow mung beans in pots, first start by filling small containers with planting soil, leaving 2 cm of space at the top. Second, plant one or two seeds about 2.5 cm deep and cover them with a thin layer of soil. Third, thoroughly water the soil until it is damp. Fourth, place the pots on a sunny place, such as windowsill or under a sufficient grow light because mung beans need at least six hours of sunlight daily. Do not overly water the mung beans, but keep the soil consistently moist by watering only when the top feels dry. After a few days, the seeds will start to grow and small sprouts will appear. Then, record their growth by noting important changes such as the appearance of leaves. If the plants outgrow their pots, transplant them into even larger containers or right in the ground when conditions are suitable. Lastly, keep watering and providing sunlight until the plants produce flowers and beans.

My Memorable Trip to Mount Bromo

Last holiday, I had an unforgettable trip to Mount Bromo with my family. It was my first time visiting East Java, and I couldn’t wait to see the famous sunrise at Mount Bromo. We prepared everything a week before, such as jackets, gloves, and scarves, because we knew it would be very cold there.

We left our hotel at midnight because the journey to the viewpoint took about two hours. My family and I got into the van to take us up the mountain. The road was dark and quiet, but I was too excited to sleep. The driver dropped us off midway, and I walked the rest of the way to the top.

When we arrived at the viewpoint, there were already many people waiting for the sunrise. The temperature was freezing, and my hands felt numb, and it was a little bit hard to breathe, but the view was worth it. When the sun started to rise, the sky turned orange and pink, creating the most beautiful scenery I had ever seen. Mount Bromo looked majestic with smoke flowing from its crater.

After watching the sunrise, we took a Jeep down to the sea of sand, then went up the stairs to the volcano's crater. I immediately saw a big wave of sulphur rising from the crater's deep inside. It was tiring, but reaching the top felt amazing. I took many photos and even made a short video for my social media.

My trip to Bromo was one of the most memorable moments in my life. I learned to appreciate nature’s beauty, and I hope I can go there again someday.

The Essential Needs to Enhance Reading Comprehension in Indonesia

A survey by the Program for International Student Assessment, or PISA, in 2022 stated that even though about 75% of Indonesian children can read, most of them have trouble comprehending the text's relevance. PISA 2022 data states that 25% of students in Indonesia only reached Level 2 reading proficiency, lower than OECD’s (the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development) average, which is 74%. At a minimum, these students can identify the main idea in a text of moderate length, find information based on explicit and complex criteria, and reflect on the purpose as well as the form of texts when clearly instructed to do so. However, the survey, which was conducted every three years, revealed that Indonesian students’ reading skills have a serious literacy issue where the majority of students are incapable of using higher-order cognitive abilities, such as interpretation and analysis.

Indonesia’s literacy problem is not simply about teaching children to read but ensuring they can comprehend and critically apply the knowledge that they get from reading. Indonesia needs systematic reform as a necessity to boost students’ ability to understand what they read and how it relates to their lives and is relevant to their practical skills. This problem is further exacerbated by the disparity in educational quality between regions. Students in underdeveloped provinces have little access to trained educators, learning materials, and educational facilities. At the institutional level, Indonesian schools have fewer freedoms in decision-making, in which fewer principals have responsibility for teacher hiring and fewer educators have the authority to decide on educational resources. These systemic weaknesses contribute to reduced literacy performances.

In conclusion, the PISA 2022 results confirm that weak reading comprehension, regional inequality, and systemic shortcomings remain major obstacles. Therefore, Indonesia must strengthen teacher training, improve school autonomy, and ensure equal access to quality resources to create meaningful improvements in literacy.

(Adapted from various sources.)

The Fairy Tale of Amat Mude

A long time ago in the Land of Alas, there lived a wise and fair king and queen who were admired by their people. One day, the royal couple was joyful that the queen had given birth to a son named Amat Mude. Sadly, the king died while Amat Mude was still a baby. Raja Mude, the king's younger brother, was chosen as a temporary ruler. However, he was harsh, envious, and greedy. In order to obtain complete authority over the Land of Alas, he exiled the queen and Amat Mude to a faraway forest. There they lived in a hut.

The former queen raised Amat Mude with love and moral principles despite the difficulties. Amat Mude grew into a kind, bright, and attractive young man, not to mention he was also a proficient fisherman. Amat Mude’s mother never lacked fish to sell in the market near the forest where they lived. One day in the market, Amat Mude’s mother was recognized by a wealthy merchant who was an old friend of the previous king. Amat Mude’s mother gave the biggest fish she had to the merchant and told him to give it to his wife as a token for their families’ friendship. When the merchant’s wife cut the fish to cook it, she discovered golden eggs inside. Realizing that this fortune was not their family’s alone but also Amat Mude’s and his mother’s, the merchant couple helped build a better house for Amat Mude and the former queen. The merchant couple also restored some of their wealth and elevated their status. Amat Mude’s new status made him even more loved and respected by the people from all over the kingdom.

Meanwhile, the news of Amat Mude’s virtues reached Raja Mude. This made him disturbed by the people’s regard of their success and worried because he thought Amat Mude could reclaim his legitimate reign. Hoping to get rid of him, Raja Mude ordered Amat Mude to get some ivory coconuts from a dangerous island inhabited by wild creatures. Amat Mude bravely sailed through storms to reach the island. He encountered mystical beings: a magical golden fish, a gigantic crocodile, and a dragon. Instead of attacking him, they helped him reach the island. On the shore, Amat Mude met a lovely young woman named Putri Niwer Gading. The woman said that she was cursed to stay forever on the shore and could only be released by drinking the ivory coconut water. Amat Mude vowed to help her.

Through thorny forests and ravaging beasts, Amat Mude successfully reached the ivory coconut tree, which had many magical fruit. A modest man, Amat Mude only plucked off enough fruit to be given to Putri Niwer Gading, his mother, and Raja Mude. Back on the shore, he gave Putri Niwer Gading her share of ivory coconut. In gratitude, she declared that she would marry him. They then sailed to go back home. Safely returned, Amat Mude made his way back to his mother and presented her share of ivory coconut. His mother opened the fruit, and out came gold coins bursting from the fruit. Amat Mude’s mother used a small portion of the gold to celebrate his son’s wedding. She invited people from far and wide to a feast to share her joy.

Finally, it’s time for Amat Mude to face Raja Mude. He came to the palace with his mother, his new bride, and Raja Mude’s share of the ivory coconut. Initially angered seeing the fruit and ready to fight, Raja Mude was taken aback when he realized that he could not harm Amat Mude. Raja Mude then repented for his actions and relinquished the throne back to Amat Mude. The restored queen and Amat Mude then forgave him. Soon after, Amat Mude became the rightful king of Alas.

questions.question: Multiple-categorization questions (24 to 25). Categorize each other statement by ticking (P) the correct column. Which of the following statements are True or False ?

Pembahasan: Pernyataan A benar karena cerita rakyat memang mengajarkan nilai moral, seperti kesabaran, kerendahan hati, kehormatan, dan keberanian melalui tokoh Amat Mude. Pernyataan B salah. Cerita The Fairy Tale of Prince Amat Mude bukanlah catatan sejarah atau kisah nyata tentang raja-raja yang pernah memimpin di Tanah Alas. Ini adalah dongeng rakyat ( folktale ) yang penuh dengan unsur magis, tokoh khayalan, dan pelajaran moral. Jadi, tujuannya bukan memberi informasi sejarah, melainkan menyampaikan nilai-nilai moral lewat cerita fiksi. Pernyataan C benar karena selain menyampaikan pesan moral, dongeng seperti ini juga memiliki tujuan utama, yaitu untuk menghibur pembaca.

Pada paragraf 4 tertulis: “Through thorny forests and ravaging beasts, Amat Mude successfully reached the ivory coconut tree …” , kalimat tersebut menyimpulkan bahwa “ ravaging beasts ” justru menjadi rintangan, bukan penolong. A Day at Music Festival

Two weeks ago, I enjoyed a music festival with some of my friends. We had been anticipating the event for months, and we were really excited to watch our favorite singers perform live.

When we got at the festival, we were met by an immense crowd of people. A lot of stages put up, with each featuring a different performer. We strolled around, checking out the various stages before settling on a location near the main stage.

The first performance was a local band, and they were fantastic. We danced and sang along with their song. After their performance, we grabbed some dinner from a food truck and continued to enjoy the festival.

As the day progressed, more people arrived, and the atmosphere became even more lively. We watched some incredible performances by famous musicians and even heard some new music that we enjoyed.

Our favorite band's performance was one of the festival's highlights. We had waited months for this moment, and it was worth the wait. They performed all their good songs, and we sang along at the top of our lungs.

As the night progressed, the music festival began to wind down. We were exhausted but delighted. We'd spent the day listening to excellent music, eating delicious food, and hanging out with our friends. It was an incredible experience that we will always remember.

(Adapted from www.detik.com/edu/detikpedia/d-6684414/7-contoh-recount-text-singkat-bahasa-inggris-dengan-terjemahannya)
